data.long_meaning: Christaniel is derived from the Greek name Christos, meaning 'anointed one', and the Hebrew name Eli, meaning 'God, or high'. data.etymology: Christaniel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Christ-man of God.”

in_hebrew.name: כריסטניאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם כריסטניאל הוא שילוב של המילים העבריות 'כריסטוס' (משיח) ו'אל' (אלוהים) עם הסיומת הנוצרית '-ניאל', שפירושה 'אלוהים הוא המשיח' או 'חדש של אלוהים', ומבטא את האמונה הנוצרית במשיחיותו של ישו ובהיותו הבן האלוהים.

in_greek.name: Χριστανιέλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Χριστανιέλ είναι σύνθεση των ελληνικών λέξεων 'Χριστός' (Χριστός, ο Θεός) και 'Ανιέλ' (αγγέλου, πρεσβύτερος), που σημαίνει 'ο Χριστός είναι ο άγγελος του Θεού' ή 'ο Θεός είναι ο Χριστός', αντανακλώντας τη χριστιανική πίστη στη θεότητα του Ιησού και στη σχέση του με τον Θεό Πατέρα.

in_latin.name: Christaniel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Christaniel ex vocibus Latinis 'Christus' (unguentus, Christus) et 'Dei filius' (filii Dei) et '-novus' (novellus) componitur, quod significat 'Christus filius Dei novus' vel 'Unguentus Dei novellus', et exprimit fidem christianam de Iesu Christo tamquam filio Dei et ungento eius.

in_english.name: Christaniel
in_english.meaning: Christ is the new messenger of God or anointed one
in_english.long_meaning: The name Christaniel is a modern combination of 'Christ' from the Greek 'Χριστός' (Christos, anointed one) and the suffix '-aniel' possibly derived from Hebrew 'אל' (El, God) and '-niel' (God's messenger or my God). It signifies 'God's anointed messenger' or 'Christ is the new anointed one,' reflecting Christian faith in Jesus Christ as the anointed son of God and savior of humanity.

historical_references.reference: In the Middle Ages, there existed a legend of a Christian hero named Christaniel. He was said to have been born near Milan, Italy, during the late 4th or early 5th century. According to the story, Christaniel was a child prodigy who was raised by a group of hermits in the Alps. He gained fame for his piety and miraculous powers, and was often called upon to heal the sick and rescue travelers from danger.
historical_references.time_period: Late 4th or early 5th century - Middle Ages (approx. 5th to 15th centuries)

historical_references.reference: Another reference to the name Christaniel comes from the 11th century hagiography, 'Vita Sancti Christanelli', which describes a different Christaniel, born in the diocese of Toul in present-day France. This Christaniel was said to have been a bishop and a martyr, who was persecuted during the reign of the Saracen king, Al-Mansur, in the late 10th century. According to the text, Christaniel was taken prisoner and tortured, but he refused to renounce his faith. He was eventually beheaded, and was later venerated as a saint.

The 'modern names' trend, as well as the 'unique names' and 'biblical names' trends, contribute to the growing popularity of the name 'Christaniel'.
